title: Python IndentationError
what: Python uses strict indentation (typically 4 spaces) to define code blocks.
why: Mixed tabs and spaces in the file.
Missing indentation under def, if, for, while, or class.
Accidental space at the beginning of an empty line.
fix: Ensure every line inside a block has identical indentation.
Configure your code editor to show invisible whitespace.
code:
def my_function():
    # Exactly 4 spaces
    value = 42
    return value

title: Python NameError: Identifier Not Defined
what: Python cannot locate the specified variable, function, or module in the local or global namespace.
why: Typo or casing mismatch in the variable name.
Using a variable before assigning it.
Forgot to import a standard or third-party module.
Variable was defined inside an inner scope (function/loop) that finished.
fix: Ensure the assignment statement executes before referencing the variable.
Add the missing import at the top of the file.
code:
import math
# Ensure variable or module exists before use
result = math.sqrt(16)

title: Python ModuleNotFoundError
what: The active Python interpreter cannot find the requested package or module in its sys.path.
why: Package is not installed in the currently active virtual environment.
Your editor is pointing to a different Python interpreter (e.g. global vs venv).
Typo in the package name or module path.
fix: Run 'pip install <package>' in your active terminal.
Verify which interpreter VS Code or your IDE is using (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P > Select Interpreter).
Check for a virtualenv activation (source venv/bin/activate).
code:
# In terminal:
python -m pip install requests
# Then in Python:
import requests

pattern: indexerror|list index out of range|string index out of range
title: Python IndexError: Sequence Index Out of Range
what: You tried to access an item at an index that does not exist in the list or string.
why: Remember indexes start at 0, so the last valid index is len(arr) - 1.
Loop index overshot the array boundaries.
fix: Check len(my_list) before accessing by index.
Use safe iteration: 'for item in my_list:' instead of indexing.
Use slicing (my_list[:1]) which never raises IndexError.

title: Python KeyError: Missing Dictionary Key
what: You attempted to access a dictionary key that does not exist in the dictionary.
why: The key is absent from the input payload or API response.
Spelling, casing, or whitespace mismatch in the string key.
Assuming nested dictionaries always exist without checking.
fix: Use dict.get(key, default) for safe retrieval with a fallback.
Check 'if key in my_dict:' before direct square-bracket access.
Use collections.defaultdict if building grouped structures.
code:
# Safe lookup with default fallback
user_name = user_data.get('name', 'Anonymous')
# Safe check
if 'email' in user_data:
    send_email(user_data['email'])

title: Python ZeroDivisionError
what: A math calculation attempted to divide a number by zero or perform modulo by zero.
why: The denominator variable was 0 or evaluated to 0.
Missing validation for user-provided numbers or empty counts.
fix: Check whether the denominator is non-zero before dividing.
Return a sensible fallback (0 or float('nan')) when the count is zero.

pattern: typeerror.*can only concatenate str|typeerror.*unsupported operand type
title: Python TypeError: Unsupported Operand Type
what: An operation was performed on two incompatible data types (e.g., adding an integer to a string).
why: Implicit type mixing (e.g. str + int without explicit casting).
A function returned None instead of a number/string.
Input from input() is always a string.
fix: Convert variables explicitly with str(), int(), or float().
Use f-strings for string formatting instead of plus concatenation.
Inspect types with type(x) or print debugging.
code:
# Clean f-string interpolation
age = 25
message = f"User age is {age}"

title: Python AttributeError: 'NoneType' Object Has No Attribute
what: You tried to call a method or access a field on a variable whose value is None.
why: A function that does not return anything (like list.sort()) returned None.
A database query or dictionary .get() returned None because the record was not found.
An exception was swallowed or caught incorrectly.
fix: Verify that the function returns a value (e.g. use sorted(list) instead of list.sort()).
Add a guard clause: 'if obj is not None:' before accessing properties.
Trace where the variable was assigned to see why it evaluates to None.
code:
# Guard against None before accessing methods
user = get_user(user_id)
if user is not None:
    print(user.name)

title: Python ValueError: Invalid Literal for Integer
what: int() function received a string that does not represent a valid base-10 integer.
why: The string contains non-numeric characters, letters, or punctuation.
The string is empty or contains only whitespace.
Passing a float string (like '3.14') directly to int().
fix: Convert float strings via float() first: int(float('3.14')).
Wrap in try...except ValueError to handle bad user inputs gracefully.

title: Python FileNotFoundError: No Such File or Directory
what: The Python script attempted to open or read a file at a path that does not exist.
why: Relative paths are evaluated relative to where you ran the command, not the script location.
Typo in the filename or file extension (.txt vs .json).
The file was deleted, moved, or not yet created.
fix: Use pathlib.Path(__file__).parent to build paths relative to the current script.
Print the current working directory with os.getcwd() to inspect where Python is looking.
Check if the file exists using Path(file).exists() before opening.
code:
from pathlib import Path
# Guaranteed relative to current script
file_path = Path(__file__).parent / 'data.json'
if file_path.exists():
    content = file_path.read_text()

title: Python RecursionError: Maximum Recursion Depth Exceeded
what: A recursive function called itself repeatedly without hitting a termination condition.
why: Missing or unreachable base case in recursive logic.
Recursive argument does not decrease or advance toward the base condition.
Accidental mutual recursion between two functions.
fix: Verify your base case condition (e.g. if n <= 0: return).
Ensure input decreases toward the base case with every call.
Refactor deep recursion to an iterative loop with a while condition.

title: Python UnboundLocalError: Referenced Before Assignment
what: A variable inside a function is assigned somewhere in the function, causing Python to treat it as local, but it was read before the assignment.
why: Assigning to a global variable inside a function without the 'global' keyword.
Re-using the same variable name inside an exception or branch.
fix: Pass the variable as an argument to the function and return its updated value.
Use the 'global' or 'nonlocal' keyword if modifying an outer variable is strictly intended.
Initialize the local variable at the very start of the function.
code:
counter = 0
def increment():
    global counter
    counter += 1

pattern: typeerror.*'nonetype' object is not iterable|'int' object is not iterable
title: Python TypeError: Object Is Not Iterable
what: You attempted to loop over (for x in obj) or unpack an object that does not support iteration.
why: A function returned None instead of an empty list or tuple.
Trying to iterate over an integer or float instead of a range().
Unpacking a single value into multiple variables.
fix: Ensure the function returns [] or () on empty cases instead of None.
Use range(n) if looping n times over a number.
Check if obj is iterable with 'isinstance(obj, (list, tuple, dict, set))'.
code:
# Safe iteration with fallback list
items = get_items() or []
for item in items:
    print(item)

pattern: cuda out of memory|out of memory.*tried to allocate
title: PyTorch CUDA Out of Memory (GPU OOM)
what: Your model, tensors, and batch activations exceeded the GPU VRAM capacity.
why: Batch size is too large for the available GPU VRAM.
Tensors accumulating in computational graph without .detach().
Model not freed between validation passes.
fix: Reduce training batch size (e.g. from 64 to 32 or 16).
Use torch.cuda.empty_cache() and wrap evaluation in 'with torch.no_grad():'.
Enable gradient accumulation or mixed precision (torch.cuda.amp.autocast()).
code:
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(inputs)
# Free VRAM cache
torch.cuda.empty_cache()

pattern: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied|size mismatch
title: PyTorch Tensor Shape Mismatch in Matrix Multiplication
what: The inner dimensions of two tensors do not match for matrix multiplication (e.g. (A, B) x (C, D) requires B == C).
why: Linear layer in_features does not match previous layer's output channels.
Forgot to flatten a convolutional feature map before passing to a linear layer.
Batch dimension was squeezed or permuted incorrectly.
fix: Print tensor shapes before the forward call with print(x.shape).
Ensure linear in_features equals previous layer output dimension.
Use nn.Flatten() between Conv2d and Linear layers.
code:
# Add flatten layer before Dense/Linear
x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
x = self.fc(x)

title: Pandas SettingWithCopyWarning
what: You are trying to modify a slice of a DataFrame rather than the original DataFrame itself.
why: Chained indexing like df['col'][0] = 5 instead of .loc.
Operating on a filtered subset without explicitly creating a .copy().
fix: Call .copy() when creating a subset DataFrame: sub_df = df[df.a > 0].copy().
code:
# Proper assignment with .loc
df.loc[df['status'] == 'active', 'priority'] = 1

title: JS TypeError: Cannot Read Properties of Undefined/Null
what: Attempted to access a property or method on a variable that currently holds null or undefined.
why: Async API request or database query returned null.
Component rendered before data finished fetching.
fix: Provide a fallback with nullish coalescing (user?.name ?? 'Guest').
code: const userName = user?.profile?.name ?? 'Guest';

title: JS ReferenceError: Variable Is Not Defined
what: The JavaScript engine cannot find the identifier in the current execution scope.
why: Typo or casing mismatch in the variable name.
Variable was declared with let/const inside a different block.
fix: Declare the variable with const or let before using.
Check import at top of file.
code:
import { calculateTotal } from './utils';
const total = calculateTotal(items);

title: JS TypeError: Value Is Not a Function
what: Function-call syntax () was used on a variable that is not a callable function.
why: Import default vs named export mismatch.
Variable was overwritten by another value.
fix: Verify named export with { func } vs default export.

title: JS TypeError: Assignment to Constant Variable
what: A variable declared with 'const' cannot be reassigned with '='.
why: Attempting to rebind a const variable in a loop or setter.
fix: Change 'const' to 'let' if the variable needs to be reassigned.
Mutate properties instead of reassigning if working with objects.
code:
let counter = 0;
counter += 1;

title: JS RangeError: Maximum Call Stack Size Exceeded
what: A function invoked itself repeatedly without hitting a base stopping condition.
why: State update inside React useEffect without dependency array.
fix: Add strict base case: if (n <= 0) return;

pattern: unexpected token '<'|is not valid json|unexpected end of json
title: JS SyntaxError: JSON.parse Failure (Unexpected Token)
what: JSON parser received invalid JSON, typically an HTML 404/500 error page from an API.
why: API returned HTML error page instead of JSON.
Trailing commas or unquoted keys in JSON.
fix: Inspect raw text with await response.text() before parsing.
Verify API route is correct and returns 200 OK.

title: CORS / Network Error: Failed to Fetch
what: The browser or runtime could not connect to the remote server or was blocked by CORS.
why: Backend server is not running on target port.
Mixed content HTTP on HTTPS page.
fix: Verify backend dev server is running.
Enable CORS middleware on backend server.

title: TypeScript TS2322: Type 'A' is not assignable to type 'B'
what: Assigned a value whose type does not match the variable or property annotation.
fix: Align types using type narrowing, type assertions, or union types.
code:

# 1. Resolve conflict in editor

pattern: cannot connect to the docker daemon|is the docker daemon running
title: Docker Daemon Not Running
what: The Docker CLI cannot communicate with the Docker background service socket.
why: Current user lacks permission to access /var/run/docker.sock.
fix: Start Docker Desktop from your applications.
On Linux: sudo systemctl start docker.
Add user to docker group: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER.
code:
sudo systemctl start docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

pattern: port is already allocated|bind: address already in use
title: Docker Port Already In Use
what: A container attempted to bind to a host port that is already being used by another service.
why: Another Docker container or local server is running on the same port (e.g. 5432, 3000, 80).
fix: Find process on port: lsof -i :<port> (or netstat -ano on Windows).
Stop the existing container with: docker stop <container-id>.
Map to a different host port: -p 8081:80.
code:
docker ps
docker stop <old_container_id>

pattern: duplicate key value violates unique constraint|unique constraint
title: SQL Unique Constraint Violation
what: An INSERT or UPDATE attempted to save a value in a column marked UNIQUE that already exists.
why: User email or primary key already present.
fix: Use upsert: ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE (Postgres) or ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (MySQL).

pattern: violates foreign key constraint|foreign key constraint fails
title: SQL Foreign Key Constraint Violation
what: A record references an ID in another table that does not exist, or a referenced parent is being deleted.
why: Parent record was not created yet.
fix: Configure ON DELETE CASCADE or ON DELETE SET NULL if intended.
code:
ALTER TABLE orders
ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user
FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id)
ON DELETE CASCADE;

title: SQL Database Deadlock Detected
what: Two concurrent transactions are waiting on locks held by each other, causing a circular block.
why: Transactions updating the same rows in reverse order.
fix: Ensure all transactions update tables and rows in a consistent order.
Keep database transactions short and fast.
